# Structured data

`business.json` is the only place the business identity is written down: name,
phone, email, postal address, geo coordinates, opening hours, areas served and
social profiles. Everything else is generated from it.

`../build-schema.py` stamps the generated blocks into every page between these
markers:

    <!-- seo:schema:start (generated by seo/build-schema.py - do not edit) -->
    <!-- seo:schema:end -->

Run it from the repo root after changing `business.json`, adding a page, or
moving a page between categories:

    python3 seo/build-schema.py            # rewrite
    python3 seo/build-schema.py --check     # exit 1 if any page is stale (CI)

It is idempotent: a second run reports 0 pages rewritten.

## What is generated

| Type | Where | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `BreadcrumbList` | every page | file path + category map in the script |
| `LocalBusiness` | `index.html` | `business.json` (incl. geo, opening hours, areaServed) |
| `Organization` | `index.html` | `business.json` |
| `WebSite` | `index.html` | `business.json` |

The homepage carries the contact section (`/#contact`), so it is also the
contact page for `LocalBusiness` purposes; there is no separate contact URL.

## What is page-owned

`Product`, `FAQPage` and `CollectionPage` blocks stay inline on their page,
because their content is page-specific. The script still processes them: it
regenerates each `Product.seller` / `Service.provider` from `business.json` so
NAP stays consistent across all 33 product pages, and it strips the banned
properties below.

## Never emitted

`aggregateRating`, `review`, `ratingValue`, `reviewCount`.

The site previously published `"ratingValue": "4.8", "reviewCount": "120"` and
review bodies attributed to a "Satisfied Customer" on the homepage. There is no
verified review data behind those numbers, and fabricated review markup risks a
manual action. The script strips these properties from every JSON-LD block on
every page on each run, so they cannot reappear by hand-editing a page.

If real reviews are collected later, they belong in a Google Business Profile,
not in hand-written markup.
